26694858df022b54: PETALING JAYA: PAS berkemungkinan akan terus bekerjasama dengan Wawasan pimpinan Hamzah Zainudin sekiranya pembatalan pendaftaran Perikatan Nasional dikekalkan, menurut bekas ketua penerangan Umno.

Shahril Hamdan berkata PAS akan menginginkan pakatan dengan Wawasan untuk mengimbangi Umno daripada menjadi terlalu dominan, sekiranya dua parti Melayu terbesar itu memutuskan untuk membentuk pakatan pilihan raya.

"PAS mahukan satu 'jambatan' antara mereka dan Umno, supaya ada sedikit jarak, ada sedikit cara untuk membolehkan rundingan itu lebih seimbang," kata Shahril dalam episod terkini audio siar 'Keluar Sekejap'.
Pakatan dengan Wawasan akan memberi manfaat kepada PAS, mengambil kira sejarah parti Islam itu dengan Umno di bawah Muafakat Nasional (MN), katanya.
MN ditubuhkan tujuh tahun lalu untuk menyatukan pengundi Melayu-Islam selepas Pakatan Harapan membentuk kerajaan persekutuan.
Bagaimanapun, PAS memutuskan untuk bekerjasama dengan Bersatu -- parti serpihan Umno -- dan Umno menganggapnya sebagai satu pengkhianatan.
PAS juga bertegas untuk membawa Bersatu ke dalam MN, di mana Umno menentangnya. Kerjasama itu akhirnya berakhir pada Disember 2022.
Shahril berkata pembatalan pendaftaran PN akan memberi kesan kepada Hamzah kerana ia boleh menjejaskan pengaruh parti itu.
Namun bekas menteri itu masih mempunyai pilihan, katanya.
"Apa pun yang kita fikir, dia antara operator yang unggul dan dia pandai menggunakan kemahiran dia itu," katanya.
Rakan pengacara, Zaidel Baharuddin, berkata pembatalan pendaftaran PN, sekiranya dikekalkan, akan mengurangkan kuasa tawar-menawar Hamzah secara ketara.
Ia juga boleh memudahkan rundingan antara Umno dan PAS, kerana tidak perlu lagi mengambil kira parti-parti lain dalam PN.

Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan Malaysia membatalkan pendaftaran PN awal minggu ini. Mahkamah Tinggi kemudian membenarkan penangguhan sementara menunggu semakan kehakiman selesai, lalu membolehkan PN beroperasi.
f26f7438d754b190: KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional (PN) is prepared to contest the Nov 14 Melaka election using the Pas logo if it cannot use its own.
PN election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor said the coalition had no objection to contesting under either the PN logo or Pas' moon symbol.
"We will face the Melaka polls soon. If we cannot use the PN logo, we will use the Pas logo. We are ready and have no problem with that," he said.
Sanusi, who is also Pas central election director, was speaking at the Himpunan dan Munajat Penyatuan Ummah (HIMPAK) gathering here today.
Also present were Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang, Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man and Wawasan president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin.

Sanusi welcomed the High Court's decision to grant PN a temporary stay against the Registrar of Societies' (RoS) suspension and deregistration of the coalition, saying it would allow PN to continue operating as a coalition pending a judicial review.

"Alhamdulillah, the court has granted a stay on the cancellation of PN's registration, which we consider unlawful. The court's decision gives PN room to continue functioning as a legitimate coalition," he said.
The High Court yesterday allowed PN's application to stay the RoS action pending the full disposal of its judicial review, but did not determine whether the deregistration was lawful.
The ruling came ahead of nomination day on Oct 31, with polling scheduled for Nov 14.
Sanusi said supporters of "penyatuan ummah" (Muslim unity) wanted cooperation among the parties to continue regardless of the logo used.
"In Kelantan and throughout the country, those who support Muslim unity want to see this cooperation continue, regardless of the logo used," he said.
He also expressed confidence in the electoral cooperation, claiming that the Muslim unity movement had previously helped defeat Pakatan Harapan (PH) in Johor and Negri Sembilan.
"Our cooperation under the banner of Muslim unity will bring down PH. All this will lead us into the 16th General Election as the government-in-waiting," he said.
The remarks come as PN's component parties prepare for the Melaka polls following the RoS decision to cancel the coalition's registration on Oct 20.
The court's stay allows PN to resume its political activities while the legal challenge proceeds.
78de8c1fd984597f: Most programming languages were written for human programmers, but that's about to change. University of Michigan professor Jason Mars has developed an academically ambitious language called Jac, and a runtime called Jaseci, that treats AI and AI agents as first-class entities.
Mars demonstrated the language and runtime in a talk at the All Things Open conference, held in Raleigh, North Carolina, this week.

The tools we use to create software – everything from programming languages to build toolchains – were made for human consumption. They were created before generative AI and are ill-fitted to understand agentic needs.

Currently, agents are drowning in polyglot complexity, he argued. "We're not using these tools anymore. We're using the agents, and the agents are using those tools. So I don't want new tools, but I want tools [for] my agents," he told the audience.
One big hungry language

In his talk, Mars cited Jarred Sumner, creator of the Bun framework, who spent $165,000 in Anthropic tokens to convert Bun’s Zig code into Rust earlier this year using a pre-release version of Mythos. Mard argued the heavy expense wasn't so much because the job itself was complicated; it was because everything had to be translated between two human-centered programming languages.
“Mythos is supposed to hack into our nuclear reactors and take over the planet like Skynet, but it can't translate Bun to Rust unless you spend $165,000,” he noted.

In Mars’s theory, Jac is a new type of programming language designed to “gobble up” other languages. Specifically, it's a Python-like language that integrates both the TypeScript and Python runtimes and toolchains. It compiles to Python bytecode, JavaScript, and native machine code. It can make full use of any libraries both in the PyPI and npm ecosystems.

And there’s more! Jac has also incorporated the LLVM compiler to implement Rust-style borrow checking and ownership semantics, allowing Jac code to directly benefit from these memory safety rules and performance gains. It can also import C and C++ libraries, thanks to the very same LLVM integration.
Mars also described an “eject function,” which can reverse-compile the user’s Jac code into TypeScript, Python, or C to meet corporate compliance.
One currently missing language is Java. “If you really need Java, Jac isn’t for Java,” he said.
Happy bot, happy lot
Just as Jac’s design sets out to battle ecosystem fragmentation, it also attempts to unify architectural fragmentation by defining data structures as graphs.

Instead of building and populating a database table, or creating objects from a class, the data’s attributes are defined under node keywords. The relationships among different nodes are defined by edge connections. Local program logic can still use objects, but the core data will be a graph, which can reside in local memory, a storage disk, or cloud server.

So, yeah, graph computing. Creating a graph from all your data is more work than just creating database tables and some foreign keys to tie ‘em together, but graphing saves agents a lot of work down the line, he posited. No longer will the agent have to burn tokens extracting data from databases, object blobs, JSON strings, or Python objects.

Instead of the agent fetching data hither and processing it over yonder, the agent can dispatch a “walker” to traverse the data structure and process it on the go. Multiple walkers can go down different paths of the graph, resulting in natural parallelism for faster execution.
Tidy the abstraction
For his All Things Open talk, Mars conducted a bake-off between Jac and LangGraph, an agent orchestration framework that uses Python libraries to build agents.

He asked an AI agent to use each platform to build a replica of Greptile, an AI code review tool. With Jac, the agent autonomously built a sophisticated multi-stage app that could call multiple tools in parallel.
Using LangGraph, the agent produced a crude linear state machine that could not work in parallel. It was probably weighed down by all of the tools it had to use, Mars concluded.
Mars’s takeaway from this exercise: The tools we provide the AI determine the quality of the output.

Thus far, the language and runtime have been used in a number of smaller commercial AI-related services, such as the GraphClaw multi-agent AI platform, the Skooch scheduler, and Tobu’s personal memory platform.
Whether developers and agents gravitate towards Jac’s promise as a unified language remains to be seen, but it certainly is giving other Python agent frameworks a run for their money. ®
550f1733380cda77: SINGAPORE: Singapore expanded on Friday its probe into companies linked to fires in Indonesia, asking 10 locally based firms for information about their efforts to contain blazes blamed for toxic haze covering the region.

The city-state has beefed up measures to combat the months-long blazes and has vowed legal action against companies responsible for the fires that have made regional air quality among the world's worst.

Over the past week, Singapore issued notices to 10 foreign-based companies, insisting that they deploy firefighting teams, stop burning or starting new fires in Indonesia and submit information about their links with associated companies in Indonesia and Singapore.
The information is to be reviewed by Singapore's National Environmental Agency (NEA).

In addition to these companies, the NEA is seeking information from 10 Singapore-registered firms in the palm oil or forestry industry who are involved with Indonesian land, the environmental agency said in a statement late Friday.

The information relates to "linkages with associated companies in Singapore and Indonesia, the location of land concessions owned by them as well as fire preventative measures or firefighting efforts", the statement said.

Singapore also said it would form a panel of experts comprising law firms, audit firms and investigative firms with expertise in conducting cross-border enquiries and investigations to help with its probe.

Indonesia experiences fires regularly during its dry season, and experts say years of deforestation and the draining of peatland for cultivation have rendered previously fire-resistant landscapes vulnerable.

Driven by a strong El Nino cycle and resulting drought, this year's blazes have been particularly severe, burning through nearly two million hectares, according to deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas.
The fires have raged across forests and peatlands, as well as palm oil and timber plantations supplying multinational firms.
Civil society groups have regularly accused companies of responsibility for the blazes, pointing to so-called "hotspots" in supplier plantations, sometimes called concessions.

Several companies implicated have insisted they are not behind the fires, including Singapore Exchange-listed First Resources and Singapore-registered Asia Pulp and Paper. Both are named by the NEA in the latest update on Singapore's probe.
Kuala Lumpur and Singapore again ranked within the world's top 10 most polluted major cities late Friday, according to Swiss-based air monitor IQAir.
143ee3910604188c: JASIN: Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh will remain Melaka Chief Minister should Barisan Nasional and its strategic partners win the state election next month, said Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
The BN chairman said his confidence in Rauf stemmed from his leadership record and capabilities, which he had demonstrated since serving as Umno executive secretary.
"With Datuk Rauf, what you 'order' is exactly what Melaka will get," he said when launching the BN election machinery for the Jasin parliamentary constituency at Dewan Alamanda/
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka election, with nomination day on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.
BN won 21 of the 28 seats contested in the 2021 Melaka state polls, paving the way for the coalition to form the state government, while Pakatan Harapan secured five seats and Perikatan Nasional two.
11ab83a7445e16ff: KUALA LUMPUR: Eduardo Sosa proved to be the saviour as Selangor fought back from a goal down to carve out a narrow 2-1 victory over a spirited Kuching City in the first leg of their FA Cup semi-final at the MBPJ Stadium on Friday.
The Red Giants were handed a wake-up call just nine minutes in when Ramdhan Saifullah silenced the home crowd, finishing smartly to put the underdogs ahead.
However, Selangor's response was swift as it took Argentine midfielder Sosa just 10 minutes to restore parity with a composed 19th-minute strike to settle the hosts' early nerves.

Selangor dictated the tempo after the break and were rewarded in the 58th minute. Brazilian forward Chrigor Moraes whipped in a pinpoint cross from the flank, and Sosa arrived right on cue to guide the ball past the Kuching goalkeeper for his second of the night.

For Selangor, this year's FA Cup campaign represents both a pursuit of grand heritage and a desperate bid to end a prolonged silverware drought. The Klang Valley outfit are currently tied with Kedah and Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT) atop the all-time roll of honour with five titles (1991, 1997, 2001, 2005, and 2009).
Yet it has been 17 long years since they last hoisted the trophy, having endured heartbreak in the 2018 final against Pahang (4-2) and a crushing 6-1 drubbing by JDT in the 2024 showpiece.

Despite the first-leg defeat, Kuching City remain firmly in the tie. Founded just 11 years ago as an amateur outfit in the state league, the "Cats" have punched well above their weight to reach back-to-back semi-finals, following their 4-1 aggregate defeat to eventual champions JDT at this same stage last season.
Meanwhile in Bandar Seri Begawan, powerhouses JDT put one foot in the final after registering a 2-0 win over DPMM at the Hassanal Bolkiah National Stadium.
Prolific hitman Bergson da Silva broke the deadlock for the Southern Tigers in the 21st minute with a trademark clinical finish.

DPMM battled bravely to keep the deficit manageable, but JDT's relentless pressure paid off in the 72nd minute when defensive midfielder Eddy Israfilov doubled the visitors' tally, leaving the Bruneian outfit with a mountain to climb.
56cdd53f2bd4dc15: PETALING JAYA: U Mobile akan membawa Jelajah ULTRA5G ke Kuantan, Kota Bharu dan Kuala Terengganu bermula hari ini hingga 7 Nov selepas mencapai 90% liputan 5G di kawasan berpenduduk di seluruh negara.
Syarikat telekomunikasi itu berkata, sasaran berkenaan dicapai sembilan bulan lebih awal daripada dijadualkan.
Jelajah ULTRA5G: Edisi Pantai Timur menawarkan pengalaman digital interaktif, demonstrasi teknologi 5G, aktiviti kecerdasan buatan (AI) dan persembahan artis Sharul Kamal serta Tomok.
Menurut syarikat telekomunikasi itu, pengunjung berpeluang berinteraksi dengan robot humanoid berteknologi 5G serta mengenali produk dan perkhidmatannya.
Jelajah bermula di Kuantan hari ini, termasuk di pusat beli-belah, pasar dan Esplanade Kuantan. Acara berasingan akan berlangsung di TC Uptown, Teluk Cempedak, esok.

1a22139c2205f5a4: JOHOR BARU: A family's plans to celebrate a 7-year-old boy's birthday next week were shattered when he died after falling from the 10th floor of their home at the Sungai Melana Phase 2 People's Housing Project (PPR) in Tampoi here.

His mother, Norhidayah Yacob, 30, said the family had planned to celebrate Mohammad Adib Rizqy Mohammad Fauzi's birthday yesterday but had to postpone it because her husband, Mohammad Fauzi Zurin, 31, who works as a lorry attendant, had yet to receive his salary.
"We had planned to celebrate my son's birthday next Tuesday, as it is also my husband's birthday.
"However, we accept what has been decreed by Allah. My son also passed away on this blessed Friday," she said when met at the scene.
The housewife said she was tidying up the house when the incident occurred, while her husband was away at work.
She learnt of the incident after one of her son's friends informed her.
"At first, I thought my son's friend was joking. When I went out and looked down from upstairs, I saw my son on the ground floor.
"I rushed downstairs and trembled when I saw that he was no longer moving before calling my husband to tell him what had happened," she said.
The victim, a Standard One pupil at SK Tampoi Utama, fell from the 10th floor of the PPR block around 5.30pm.
His body was sent to Hospital Sultanah Aminah here for a post-mortem.
60f45a4a096c6872: KUALA LUMPUR: Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim menyuarakan kekecewaan melihat 'pemikiran jumud' di Parlimen, sedangkan negara memerlukan wakil rakyat berbincang isu ekonomi dan industri.

Anwar membidas perbincangan yang masih terikat dengan pemikiran jumud ketika negara hendak 'menggapai langit' dengan menguasai teknologi kecerdasan buatan (AI), superkomputer, dan pengkomputeran berprestasi tinggi.
"Tanpa menguasai ini, kita hanya akan ketinggalan, dan ini masalah besar bagi negara kita," katanya dalam ucapan sempena majlis Anugerah Kecemerlangan Industri di Menara Miti.

"Kalau lihat umpamanya perdebatan di Parlimen sekarang, yang diutamakan ialah... tak ada langsung. Perbincangan itu -- 'siapa Islam', 'siapa tak Islam', 'siapa munafik', 'siapa tidak' -- masih lagi terikat dengan kerangka pemikiran jumud, lama, dan kolot."

Anwar merujuk kepada tema Belanjawan 2027 yang dibentangkan di Parlimen baru-baru ini, "Malaysia MADANI: Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi". Bajet itu antara lain menumpukan kepada pendigitalan, pembangunan AI, penyelidikan dan pembangunan, prasarana digital dan keselamatan, serta tenaga hijau.
Anwar bertegas bahawa martabat ekonomi negara tidak boleh diangkat dengan 'pendekatan lama yang kaku'.
"Kalau negara ini mahu dibangunkan, mestilah ada kesediaan generasi baharu dan pihak industri untuk memiliki keupayaan.
Pada masa sama, Anwar mengingatkan bahawa Malaysia sebuah negara majmuk, dengan pelbagai kaum, agama, sentimen, dan wilayah.
"Bahasa kita, budaya kita, adab kita, kemanusiaan kita -- menghormati sentimen pelbagai kaum, pelbagai agama kerana ini suatu keperluan -- satu imperatif yang tidak boleh kita pinggirkan," katanya.
"Sebab itu kita kata menggapai di langit, tetapi mengakar ke bumi," katanya.
Seterusnya, Anwar menyorot perhatian hadirin kepada kepentingan menyokong puluhan ribu perusahaan kecil dan sederhana (PKS) agar keupayaan mereka setara dengan semangat keusahawan yang tinggi.
Anwar melihat PKS sebagai penentu penting dalam memajukan negara.

"Kalau puluhan ribu SME ini terangkat kedudukan dia menjadi pemain industri yang penting -- kecekalan dia, inovasinya, daya cipta yang kita dukung -- dan kemudian dapat kejayaan untuk menembusi pasaran antarabangsa...penentu kan?
"Maka Kementerian Kewangan, dan saya dalam belanjawan, memutuskan untuk memberikan fokus dalam bentuk pinjaman, penyuntikan, dan beberapa insentif yang telah diperkenalkan," katanya.
7cc9260175059f40: PETALING JAYA: PAS would likely continue working with Hamzah Zainudin's Wawasan in the event Perikatan Nasional's deregistration is upheld, a former Umno information chief said.

Shahril Hamdan said PAS would want an alliance with Wawasan as the latter would help prevent Umno from becoming too dominant in the event the two largest Malay parties decide to forge an electoral pact.
"PAS would want to maintain some distance (from Umno) and have more balanced (seat) negotiations," Shahril said in the latest episode of the Keluar Sekejap podcast.
An alliance with Wawasan, he said, would benefit PAS, given the Islamic party's history with Umno under Muafakat Nasional.
MN was established seven years ago to consolidate the Malay-Muslim vote after Pakatan Harapan formed the federal government.

However, PAS decided to work with Bersatu – an Umno splinter party – to form PN following the fall of the PH government, leading to the appointment of Muhyiddin Yassin as prime minister in 2020, which Umno viewed as a betrayal.
PAS also insisted on roping Bersatu into MN, which Umno opposed. The pact eventually ended in December 2022.
Shahril said PN's deregistration would affect Hamzah as his party could lose some political clout.
But he said the former federal minister has options.
"Whatever we may think of Hamzah, he is an outstanding political operator,” he said.
Shahril’s co-host, Muda deputy president Zaidel Baharuddin, said PN’s deregistration, if it is upheld, would considerably reduce Hamzah’s bargaining power.
It could also make negotiations between Umno and PAS more straightforward, as there is no need to accommodate the wider coalition.

The Registrar of Societies deregistered PN earlier this week, although the High Court subsequently granted a stay pending judicial review, allowing the coalition to continue operating and use its logo.
dc03a0af7e6e3e83: WASHINGTON: The US department of energy said on Friday it had authorised an emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address a supply disruption affecting Phillips 66's Lake Charles refinery in Louisiana.

The SPR has already been at the lowest level since 1982, after President Donald Trump tapped it as the US war on Iran disrupted supply lines, and after his predecessor, President Joe Biden, turned to it following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The Lake Charles refinery has a capacity to refine about 264,000 barrels per day.

The exchange will "help offset temporary disruptions affecting crude oil deliveries to the refinery and support continued production of transportation fuels serving Louisiana and surrounding markets," the department said.
Phillips 66 did not immediately respond to a request for comment about why the oil is needed.
81f1ac916327e793: The Arc browser has flatlined, with its maker announcing it will be sunsetting it altogether on December 22, 2026. The Browser Company announced the news on October 22, just over three years after we noted Arc's arrival.

Nothing will happen immediately, other than an end to new Arc accounts. Starting November 23, lights will begin turning off on iOS and Android, with several AI features disabled and sign-ins to sync tabs removed. Finally, on December 22, it will no longer be possible to access or use Arc on macOS and Windows. Accounts will be deactivated, and data deleted within 30 days.
The solution? According to The Browser Company, a move to its AI browser, Dia, is one way forward. Users can import their profiles into the brave, new AI-native world and carry on as before. Sort of.

When it launched, the Chromium-based Arc was an innovative browser with a workflow unlike its rivals. Instead of a plethora of tabs, there was a sidebar. The browser attempted to change how users interacted with the web but… frankly… it never really caught on.

The writing was on the wall for a while. In 2025, The Browser Company pivoted to AI and its Dia browser, dropping Arc into maintenance mode. Later that year, the vendor was snapped up by Atlassian, although Arc continued to plow its lonely furrow.

However, a year on, the time has come for Arc. CEO Josh Miller wrote: "We have so much pride and love for what we made alongside the Arc community," but it seems that wasn't enough to keep the browser maintained alongside Dia development.

Hopes that Arc might be open-sourced so that its community could continue development were dashed in 2025, when Miller explained that "Arc isn't just a Chromium fork … It runs on custom infrastructure we call ADK — the Arc Development Kit."

Arc's innovations have found their way, at least in part, into other browsers. Many users have found solace in the Zen browser, and there is always Vivaldi for power users. There is also a level of risk in going all-in on AI-native browsers in an increasingly crowded marketplace. For example, Strawberry, currently in beta, leverages AI agents to smooth a user's workflow. Dia might be a successor to Arc, but there is a risk that users will consider something else.
As for Arc itself, The Browser Company plans to focus on Dia going forward. So for the Arc community, it is time to move on. ®
8b57e80aee6564e9: PUTRAJAYA: Future urban development must balance technological advancement with the preservation of national heritage and identity to create comfortable, sustainable and climate-resilient cities.

Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said traditional design principles could be combined with modern technology to build homes better suited to local conditions, including hot weather and flood risks.

"Building the cities of the future does not mean setting aside our heritage and history. Instead, traditional design wisdom can be combined with modern technology to create homes that are more comfortable and resilient to hot weather and flood risks," he said at the national-level World Habitat Day celebration here today.
Nga, who is also president of the UN-Habitat Assembly, cited traditional Malay houses as an example of architecture that could inspire modern housing development.
He said features such as raised structures, natural ventilation and verandas that foster neighbourhood ties deserved greater consideration in future housing plans.
He said the Housing and Local Government Ministry encouraged the development of affordable homes near public transport and employment centres to ease daily commutes and improve quality of life.
Housing plans should also consider access to jobs, basic amenities, green spaces and community services to ensure residents could afford their homes and enjoy a conducive living environment, he said.
"Under the Malaysia Madani framework, a home is not merely a commodity, but a basic necessity that forms the foundation of the people's well-being," he said.

Nga said Malaysia was also strengthening its commitment to energy-efficient and climate-responsive housing through the IPOH Accord, finalised at the Fourth Asean-China Ministerial Roundtable Conference on Housing (ACMROCH).

This year's World Habitat Day carries the national theme "The Future City I Want to Live In", reflecting aspirations for cities that account for climate change, cultural heritage, development experiences and Malaysia's diverse communities.
At the event, Nga presented the Malaysia 2026 Honorary Scroll Award and the MUF 2026 Future City Pilot Project Award in recognition of contributions to improving urban well-being.
World Habitat Day was designated by the United Nations General Assembly to raise awareness of everyone's right to adequate shelter.
4877edd1dc191e4f: KUALA LUMPUR: A covered pedestrian bridge linking the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) Gombak station directly to the Gombak LRT station is expected to be completed by March next year.

Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL), in a statement today, said public transport integration and pedestrian access at the ECRL Gombak Integrated Terminal (TBG) station had been considered from the early planning stages.
The covered bridge will connect the ECRL and LRT stations, with a further pedestrian link to TBG.

While awaiting completion of the permanent bridge, MRL will provide a temporary walkway through Prasarana Malaysia Bhd's facilities to allow passengers to move between the stations when ECRL services begin in December.
MRL said the temporary route would prioritise safety, comfort and ease of movement, including for passengers carrying luggage.
It was also discussing with Prasarana a proposed shuttle service between the two stations, particularly for passengers with luggage.
MRL said the access facilities were part of efforts to integrate the Gombak ECRL station with the existing rail and public transport network.
It added that temporary arrangements would be managed to meet passenger needs when services began, while the permanent bridge was completed in stages.

"MRL appreciates the attention, views and feedback from the public and will continue to collaborate with relevant parties to ensure that the facilities provided are safe, practical and user-friendly," it said. — BERNAMA
4b762a38184125d0: KOTA BARU: Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin has claimed that the Registrar of Societies (RoS) acted unlawfully by cancelling Perikatan Nasional's registration within 28 days, instead of the 30-day period stipulated by law.
Hamzah, who is also Parti Wawasan Negara president, said PN had received a letter from RoS and submitted its response within two weeks.
"The cancellation should not have been carried out before the 30-day period stipulated under the Societies Act had expired.

"The law in our country says 30 days. The home minister oversees RoS, and I know they have abused their powers by cancelling PN within 28 days. This is an injustice, and we strongly oppose it," he said at the Himpunan dan Munajat Penyatuan Ummah (Himpak) gathering at Sultan Muhammad IV Stadium.
Yesterday, the High Court allowed PN's application to stay its suspension and subsequent deregistration by the RoS on Oct 20.
Hamzah also questioned RoS's decision to appeal against the court ruling.
He said the move raised questions, as RoS was challenging a court decision concerning its own earlier action.
He added that any action against a political party for an alleged offence should follow the prescribed legal process.
He said PN was the country's largest opposition coalition and claimed that the authorities feared its influence.
"That is why I believe they are truly afraid of PN.
"We must rise and show that the people are with us in taking over the government and correcting everything they have done," he said.
32699da19a9a0516: LIVERPOOL: Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said on Friday he will not ease off his high-intensity demands despite suffering a series of injuries.

The Reds are set to be without Dominik Szoboszlai, Jeremie Frimpong and Victor Munoz for the visit of Brighton on Sunday, while Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo have recently returned from injuries picked up on international duty.

Iraola's high-energy style at Bournemouth reaped success, which earned him the job at Anfield, but for the first time in his managerial career, he is having to deal with the added toll of European football.
"The way we want to play you cannot play 70 per cent," Iraola said at his pre-match press conference.
"Imagine you don't have a right-winger on the bench, I will put someone as a right-winger. I prefer to do this than you save your energy so you have to last 90 minutes.
"Give everything for 60 minutes, 65, 70, or 72, and then someone will do the 18, 35, or whatever because we need to play full gas.
"I would like to say we are good enough to play 70% and win games, but it's not (the case). We have to play our very best because the teams we have in front of us are very good."
Liverpool go into the weekend four points adrift of third-placed Brighton, who are the Premier League's top scorers with 23 goals in seven games.
"I think they are doing incredibly well. They deserve all the praise they are getting, and I think there is little doubt there. I think it's a team that is very well coached," Iraola said.
"We have to be at our very best to beat Brighton because now they are with confidence. But I also see my team in a good place."
Szoboszlai's return from injury was cut short in last weekend's victory at Brentford, but Iraola is hopeful the Hungarian will not be sidelined for long.

"I don't think he's far, but he hasn't trained with the group still, and also, considering that we started him and he had to go out, we will probably take one or two days more than we would last week," said the Spaniard.
"He's in a good place. Dom is already training outside alone, and he's going to train with the group, but he's not ready for this one."
862d7d48ada97f63: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economic strength must rest on tens of thousands of small and medium enterprises (SMEs), rather than a handful of corporate giants.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said SMEs must be empowered to innovate, build industrial capabilities and penetrate international markets to drive economic growth.

"Our strength does not lie in a few dozen giant companies, although they are important and we work with them, but in tens of thousands of SMEs," he said at the 2026 Industry Excellence Awards here today.
Present were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Deputy Minister Sim Tze Tzin.
Anwar said a significant gap remained in SMEs' capabilities and contributions, which must be addressed if Malaysia were to become a more competitive industrial economy.
He said the 2027 Budget placed particular emphasis on strengthening SMEs through financing facilities and targeted incentives, taking into account proposals and feedback from industry players.
He said industrial progress must also create greater economic opportunities for ordinary Malaysians, warning against celebrating strong growth and export figures while inequality widened.
"We cannot talk about driving growth, high exports and impressive figures while inequality widens.
"The poor cannot be marginalised and left neglected, whether in rural areas in Kelantan or in Kapit, Sarawak. That cannot happen," he added.
Anwar said Malaysia must pursue technological advancement and industrial modernisation while remaining grounded in its national identity, cultural values and commitment to public welfare.
He also criticised Dewan Rakyat debates for dwelling on outdated issues when the country needed to master artificial intelligence (AI) and emerging technologies.
"If we look at debates in Parliament now, they are not reaching for the skies. They are discussing who is Islamic, who is not, who is a hypocrite and who is not.
"We are still bound by rigid, outdated and backward ways of thinking," he said.
Anwar said Malaysia could not afford to approach economic development with outdated thinking, stressing that industries must modernise and adapt swiftly to technological change to remain competitive.
edbc73a8b1fa92af: THE recent decision by the government to ban the use of a popular navigation application has generated considerable public discussion.

The decision is viewed as timely, given that excessive dependence on navigation technologies developed and operated through foreign expertise and infrastructure carries potential implications for national security, including the safety and privacy of ordinary citizens.
In today's digital age, driving and mobility have become increasingly dependent on navigation apps that provide real-time direction to chosen destinations.
These apps offer valuable information on traffic conditions, alternative routes, and other services designed to facilitate safer, more efficient and convenient journeys.

Digital navigation services have become deeply embedded in various aspects of everyday life. Digital mapping is no longer merely a convenience but an essential component across multiple sectors and daily activities.
Such dependence, however, must be accompanied by strong assurances of personal data protection, information security and legal safeguards enforceable under Malaysian law.
Where personal data protection arrangements and legal jurisdiction involve third countries, including, for example, Israel, the potential national security implications warrant serious scrutiny.

The world has witnessed conflicts in the Middle East involving targeted attacks and assassinations reportedly associated with the ability of foreign intelligence agencies to identify and track individuals with considerable precision. Such developments raise legitimate concerns about the potential misuse of location intelligence and other sensitive digital information.

These security risks are not necessarily confined to individuals serving in national security or defence institutions. They may also extend to professionals working in strategically critical fields, including engineering, economics and healthcare, whose expertise and contributions constitute valuable national assets.

The broader lesson from these developments is that Malaysia must continue to strengthen its domestic technological capabilities while progressively reducing excessive dependence on foreign technologies and expertise.

As acknowledged by the prime minister himself, Malaysia is not yet fully prepared. Nevertheless, this acknowledgement carries a broader message: the importance of establishing a clear national direction towards safeguarding digital sovereignty, strengthening cybersecurity and protecting both national interests and Malaysians.

In this context, efforts to develop indigenous expertise and capabilities in digital navigation deserve serious consideration and support, notwithstanding the technological, operational and institutional challenges involved.

Such efforts should not merely be regarded as an exercise in technological self-reliance. They represent an opportunity to strengthen Malaysia's strategic autonomy, cultivate domestic innovation and build the capacity to develop world-class digital solutions that are secure, credible and founded upon the highest standards of integrity.
dea2a160aca82e6a: FROM haze to Waze. Social media has been abuzz with wordplay in recent days following the government's announcement that civil servants would be barred from using the popular navigation app Waze, and encouraged to switch to the locally developed alternative TuJu.
Beyond the ban itself, the episode raises a more important question: how much control does Malaysia have over the technology it relies on?

A country aspiring to be a serious digital economy cannot afford to be overly dependent on foreign technology, particularly when essential services, sensitive data and national interests may be at stake.
Digital independence should, therefore, be a strategic priority and not merely a slogan invoked whenever a foreign platform becomes controversial.

This doesn't mean foreign technology is inherently unsafe, nor that Malaysia must develop every digital service from scratch. But excessive dependence on external providers can leave the country vulnerable to decisions, policies and geopolitical developments beyond its control. The ability to choose, develop and sustain essential digital services is an important dimension of national resilience and sovereignty.

Malaysia must, therefore, invest in building its own digital capabilities. This requires sustained funding for research and development, nurturing local talent, strengthening cybersecurity, expanding cloud infrastructure and data centres, and protecting home-grown intellectual property.
It also means creating the conditions for Malaysian technology companies to grow into commercially viable businesses, rather than relying indefinitely on government backing or preferential treatment.

Yet digital independence cannot be achieved simply by directing Malaysians to use local products. Domestic alternatives must be capable of meeting public needs before they can reasonably replace established foreign platforms.

Protectionist measures may offer fledgling industries breathing space, but shielding local products from competition without demanding performance risks creating dependency of another kind — on government mandates rather than public confidence. TuJu's emergence has brought these competing considerations into focus.
While a local navigation app is preferable in principle, its domestic origins alone cannot guarantee it is a suitable replacement for Waze.

Its initial spell in the limelight has so far done little to inspire confidence. Before TuJu can be expected to win over a wider user base, it must demonstrate that its navigation is reliable, its traffic information accurate and timely, and its approach to privacy and data governance robust and transparent.
The government should be clear about the distinction between encouraging local innovation and compelling the public to accept a product that has yet to prove itself.

Civil servants, like other users, need tools that work consistently and meet their operational needs. A domestic alternative that falls short will struggle to earn trust, regardless of the policy behind its adoption.

Ultimately, the objective must be to build a Malaysian digital ecosystem that can compete on merit, serve the country's interests and reduce vulnerabilities arising from excessive reliance on foreign providers. That will take more than a ban or a change of navigation app. It demands long-term investment, sound policy and an environment in which local innovators can develop products good enough to win over users at home and abroad.
The Waze controversy should serve as a wake-up call. Malaysia needs greater digital independence, but that independence must be built on capability, credibility and quality.

Local alternatives deserve consideration, not an unconditional endorsement. Before Malaysians are asked to change course, those alternatives must first show that they can take them where they need to go.
5aa4612bc740bfce: PETALING JAYA: U Mobile will take its ULTRA5G roadshow to Kuantan, Kota Bharu and Kuala Terengganu from today to Nov 7 following its achievement of 90% 5G coverage of populated areas nationwide.
The telecommunications company said the milestone was reached more than nine months ahead of schedule.

The roadshow - Jelajah ULTRA5G: Edisi Pantai Timur - will feature interactive digital experiences, demonstrations of 5G-enabled technology, and artificial intelligence activities, as well as performances by artistes Sharul Kamal and Tomok, it said in a statement.
Visitors will also be able to interact with a 5G-enabled humanoid robot and learn more about U Mobile's products and services.
The company said the event was aimed at giving East Coast communities an opportunity to experience its ULTRA5G network and explore its offerings.
U Mobile also highlighted its free seven-day ULTRA5G eSIM trial, which comes with 10GB of 5G data.

The roadshow will begin in Kuantan today with activities at various locations around the town, including shopping malls, markets and the Kuantan Esplanade. A separate event will be held at TC Uptown in Teluk Cempedak tomorrow.
The programme will move to Bachok, Kelantan, on Oct 30, followed by activities at various locations in Kota Bharu on Oct 31.
In Terengganu, the roadshow will be held at several locations in Kuala Terengganu on Nov 6 before concluding at Teluk Ketapang beach on Nov 7.
U Mobile said its ULTRA5G network had been recognised by Ookla earlier this year as Malaysia's fastest 5G network and best mobile network.
The company described ULTRA5G as having the country's widest 5G coverage of populated areas.
3563b42c1e7e19d2: KUCHING: Artificial intelligence (AI) cannot match human wisdom and emotional intelligence in preserving cultural heritage and fostering global peace.

Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg said while technological advances provided essential data for problem-solving, human intelligence remained central to finding meaningful solutions and preserving cultural continuity.
"Even with scientific innovations such as AI, artificial intelligence cannot match human intelligence. AI has no wisdom, but humans do.

"Data is needed to find solutions, but the human brain remains superior to artificial intelligence," he said in his keynote address at the 22nd International Council on Monuments and Sites (ICOMOS) General Assembly and Scientific Symposium 2026 gala dinner here tonight.
Abang Johari said protecting heritage through human-led efforts grounded in shared values was crucial to building a peaceful world.

He said safeguarding living heritage required traditional knowledge to be combined with human wisdom, an approach reflected in Sarawak's commitment to social inclusivity and environmental sustainability under its Post-Covid-19 Development Strategy (PCDS) 2030.

The gala dinner marked the end of the week-long ICOMOS General Assembly 2026, which brought together 1,800 delegates from 110 countries and saw the adoption of the Kuching Declaration on safeguarding living heritage.
Organised by ICOMOS Malaysia in collaboration with ICOMOS International, the assembly marked the first time the prestigious global gathering was held in Southeast Asia.
2b9f74de11bd5ba5: KUALA LUMPUR: A baby boy believed to be about a month old was found alive in a box under the staircase of an apartment block in Kepong yesterday.
Gombak police chief Assistant Commissioner Ibrahim Husin said police received a report about the discovery from a man in his 30s at 9.14am.
He said the baby was believed to have been abandoned by an unidentified person under the staircase of Block 1, Desa Satu, Desa Aman Puri Apartment, Jalan Puri Kepong.
"The baby boy is in good health and has been admitted to hospital for further observation," he said in a statement.
Ibrahim said the case was being investigated under Section 317 of the Penal Code for child abandonment.
He also urged anyone with information about the incident to contact investigating officer Inspector Mohammad Hisham Mohd Rahman @ Amir Hamzah at 010-9475532 or their nearest police station.
097024fb1c8be975: LONDON: Former Chelsea and Napoli coach Antonio Conte said on Friday he was not in advanced negotiations to replace Manchester United manager Michael Carrick, and called reports that he had demanded full control at the club as "unfounded."

Conte, who won the Premier League with Chelsea and also managed Tottenham Hotspur in England, was responding to speculation that he had requested full control while also making financial demands of the struggling Old Trafford club.
United sit 13th in the Premier League and 20th in the Champions League standings following Wednesday's humiliating 4-1 thrashing by Italian side Como, increasing scrutiny on Carrick.
"My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage," Conte said in a statement.

"Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management," he added of his time in Naples where he won Serie A in the 2024-25 season.
"It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.

"I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my 'strong personality'.
"These reports are unfounded, as there is currently no concrete basis for such assessments."

Conte, who last coached Napoli in the 2025-26 season, said that if a concrete opportunity arose, he would enter talks with the club involved and "jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement", taking into account the needs of both parties.
"Until then, any assumptions about my demands and my professional future remain speculation and cannot be treated as fact," the 57-year-old Italian added.
In an interview with The Athletic earlier this month, Conte said he would like to manage a club that has "lost sight of their history" so he can help "make it shine once more."

Defeat against Como extended United's winless run to seven games in all competitions and skipper Bruno Fernandes said his team had adopted a "mood of defeat" while also questioning the tactics, with Carrick apologising for the performance.
Brighton & Hove Albion manager Fabian Huerzeler, another name linked with the United job, also distanced himself from the speculation on Friday.
The 33-year-old, England's youngest top-flight manager, said he was focused solely on Brighton, who sit third in the Premier League after a string of impressive performances.

"I have no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days and, beside that, I have a lot of respect for Michael Carrick and what he has done with Manchester United the last season," Huerzeler told a press conference.
"He's a great human being, a great personality. There's nothing more to say about that."
10697ccf3a9c37bd: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian companies must produce more components for investors to reduce import dependence and widen the country's trade surplus.

Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said exports grew 34 per cent in the first nine months of this year compared with the same period last year, while imports rose 25 per cent.
He said domestic firms, including small and medium enterprises (SMEs), could help meet investors' production needs by becoming part of their supply chains.
"When we bring in investors, they want to manufacture products. If we cannot supply the components they need, they have to import them.

"An investor may need 10 types of materials or components to manufacture a product. If three or four local companies can produce some of those components, we can reduce imports," he told reporters after the 2026 Industry Excellence Awards at the ministry's headquarters here today.
Also present were Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin.
Johari said greater domestic production would help Malaysia expand its economy and exports while slowing import growth.
He said, for example, export growth of 34 per cent alongside import growth of 10 per cent could generate a larger trade surplus if more production inputs were sourced locally.
He urged local companies to identify the components investors needed and invest in research and development (R&D) to produce them.
Earlier in his speech, Johari said the New Industrial Master Plan 2030 aimed to advance manufacturing through innovation, technology, digitalisation and automation.
He said Malaysian companies should develop their own technology, strengthen R&D and build strong brands to become trusted suppliers to multinational companies and global industry leaders.
"This progress must translate into quality job opportunities, a highly skilled workforce, as well as higher incomes and living standards for the people," he said.
Johari said the biennial awards recognised companies' economic contributions and provided benchmarks for newer businesses to learn from successful firms in the manufacturing and services sectors.
e52c9b687dde0182: WASHINGTON: US First Lady Melania Trump said in a surprise announcement Friday she had secured a localised ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the ravaged city of Oleshky, where citizens are trapped and short of food.
The localised ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky would begin on Oct 29, a statement issued by her office said. There was no immediate confirmation from Moscow or Kyiv.
"The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a frontline war city on the brink of disaster," Melania, the wife of President Donald Trump, said in the statement.
"It was abundantly clear that without my intervention, the possibility of bringing humanitarian aid into the city and of evacuating the elderly would be impossible."
The announcement comes a year after the Slovenian-born former model stunned the world by revealing she had established a back channel of communication with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Melania Trump has since secured the "reunifications" of 34 children separated from their parents by the war, her office said. In a number of cases they had been abducted by Russia.
Her announcement also comes as President Trump has stepped up efforts to end Moscow's war on Ukraine – largely by pivoting back towards Putin and away from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Melania Trump said she had worked with the Russian and Ukrainian leadership on the Oleshky plan and that civilian leaders from both countries would "work together" and visit the devastated city to assess aid needs.
"Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine," she said.

She added that she and an "impartial American media organisation" – which she did not identify – would "accompany and document Russian and Ukrainian teams on the ground throughout the process" to ensure residents' wishes were respected.

Oleshky, on the southern bank of the Dnipro River in the Kherson region, was seized by Russian troops in 2022. The population has dropped from about 24,000 before Russia invaded to around 2,000 today.
Former residents of the city told AFP earlier this month that people there were caught in the crossfire between Russia and Ukraine and facing worsening shortages of food and medication.
The 56-year-old First Lady carefully guards her image and is an infrequent presence at the White House, preferring to stay in New York, where her son Barron is studying.
But she has ramped up her public profile in recent months, launching a series of initiatives, including one to help older foster children and another to tackle online harassment.
Last week Melania Trump unveiled a women's health programme in a press conference in the White House Rose Garden alongside her husband, who lavished praise on her.
In January she released a documentary movie called "Melania", giving a manicured view of her husband's return to power. The film was funded by a multimillion-dollar deal with Amazon.
adac98b0bb388c40: TAWAU: A police inspector was sentenced to six years' imprisonment by the magistrate's court today for using forged documents in drug investigation papers three years ago.
Magistrate Dayang Aidaku Amira Aminuddin found Crall Mark Bait, 36, guilty of three amended charges under Section 471 of the Penal Code, punishable under Section 466 of the same code.
"The court is satisfied that the prosecution has proven each of the three amended charges under Section 471 of the Penal Code, punishable under Section 466 of the same code, beyond reasonable doubt.
"I therefore find the accused guilty and convict him on all three amended charges," she said in her judgement.
The accused was sentenced to two years' imprisonment for each charge, with the sentences ordered to run consecutively, bringing the total to six years.
However, the court granted a stay of execution pending an appeal following an application by his lawyer, Sylvester Kuan.

Under the three amended charges, Crall was accused of fraudulently using as genuine forged documents comprising statements recorded under Section 112 of the Criminal Procedure Code by three police personnel acting in their official capacities.

During mitigation, Sylvester urged the court to impose a lighter sentence, saying his client had been suspended from duty and was receiving only part of his basic salary, leaving him in financial difficulty.
However, Deputy Public Prosecutor Shearil Aizad Murnizam urged the court to impose a heavier sentence, citing the seriousness of the offences and the accused's position as a police officer.
77d9f92c07bd41dc: MANCHESTER: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick mounted an impassioned defence of his leadership on Friday, accepting responsibility for the club's collapse in form and saying he remains convinced he can lead the team out of their current crisis.

Carrick's position is under increasing pressure after United extended their winless run to seven matches in all competitions with Wednesday's humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como leaving them 20th in the table with three points.

Before taking questions ahead of Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth, Carrick delivered an emotional opening statement, acknowledging supporters' frustrations and the scale of the challenge facing him.
"Recently, we haven't had a good time. I think that's pretty obvious. So I totally accept what we're going through at the moment," he said.
"We had five months of relative success (last season) in a spell where I was happy with a lot of things I was seeing and that we were doing as a team," he said.
"We haven't done well enough lately. We've had a spell that we're really not happy with."
Carrick described the loss in Italy as one of the most painful nights of his tenure.
"Wednesday was a bad night. It was a bad night for a lot of reasons. It hurt a lot," he said. "It obviously hurt me to see us play that way. As I said after the game, it was really unacceptable."
The defeat intensified scrutiny of Carrick after captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to question United's tactical approach in his post-match comments.
DRESSING ROOMS CRACKS?
Asked whether public criticism from players suggested cracks within the dressing room, Carrick rejected any suggestion the squad was split.
He also sidestepped questions over Fernandes' future as captain and declined to reveal whether he had held talks with the Portugal midfielder following the defeat.
Instead, he stressed that his priority was restoring an identity that has disappeared from the side in recent weeks.
"My responsibility is to get a team on the pitch that represents this football club, represents the supporters and they can be proud of it with the identity that we show," Carrick said.
"We have gone away from that just recently in certain games, which I'm fully aware of and definitely doing something about."
He reserved special mention for United's fans, many of whom travelled to Como only to watch their side suffer the heaviest defeat of his reign.
"The supporters are a huge part of this football club. They have to make the effort and the time and money they spend, to feel how we all felt on Wednesday was a tough moment," he said.
DEFIANT TONE

Despite growing speculation about his future, Carrick struck a defiant tone, saying he remained confident United could rediscover the energy and connection that characterised last season's performances.
He took over in January 2026 after the sacking of Ruben Amorim and oversaw a remarkable turnaround, steering United to a top-three finish and Champions League qualification.
"For them (the fans) to feel like they felt for five months at the start of the year ... is something we need to get back to. We will get back to it. I fully believe that," said Carrick.

Former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea manager Antonio Conte is among the names linked with United's managerial job, although the 57-year-old Italian said on Friday he had not had any negotiations "at an advanced stage" with any club.
Carrick acknowledged that United had lost their way but said responsibility rested squarely with him.
He ended his opening remarks by saying it was his duty to guide the club back on course, describing his role as "holding the umbrella for me to get wet and everyone else to stay dry."
United are 13th in the Premier League standings on seven points, while Bournemouth are a point behind them in 15th.

991e05bacd358243: PETALING JAYA: Former Umno information chief Shahril Hamdan has questioned the timing of the government's move to ban the use of Waze among civil servants, saying the navigation app's links to Israel have been known for years.

While acknowledging national security concerns surrounding the app, Shahril questioned why concerns over Waze were only being raised now and whether the government had a serious long-term strategy to reduce Malaysia's reliance on foreign technology.

“If we have known for years that Waze is registered in Israel and continues to operate from there, why is it only becoming an issue now? Its not like we just found out two or three months ago," he asked in the latest episode of the Keluar Sekejap podcast.
Shahril said the government needed to demonstrate a genuine commitment to technological sovereignty rather than sensationalise the issue.
“If the government is serious about data sovereignty and security, and reducing our dependence on foreign technology, it needs to take meaningful action over the coming years.
“To me, there is an element of performance here,” he said.
Shahril also questioned the promotion of locally developed navigation app TuJu as an alternative to Waze, saying it was not yet ready to compete with established platforms.
He also warned against reducing the controversy to a debate over support for Israel or Palestine.

“The issue now risks becoming about who opposes the Israeli regime and who doesn't. But the issue is actually far more complex and requires a genuine commitment from the government to come up with a plan,” he said.

Co-host and Muda deputy president Zaidel Baharuddin, however, defended the push for locally developed navigation technology, saying Malaysia should not abandon efforts to develop TuJu because of its early shortcomings.

He acknowledged the app's technical weaknesses but noted that platforms such as Waze and Google Maps became more effective as their user bases grew, enabling them to provide more accurate real-time traffic data.
Zaidel said developing local geospatial technology was particularly important for national security, especially for sensitive operations involving the armed forces and police.

“I believe that when it comes to technological sovereignty, the armed forces and police should not use foreign geospatial technology for official duties, as the information involved is extremely sensitive,” he said.
Zaidel maintained that TuJu's shortcomings should be addressed without abandoning the broader goal of strengthening Malaysia's technological sovereignty.
7e1090e818b11134: SparkyOS is a novel distro from the folks behind SparkyLinux: it's a version of Arch that can you can use without installing it at all.

SparkyOS is a new distro from the team behind the Debian-based SparkyLinux, but it's quite different. SparkyOS is based on Arch, and it runs entirely from USB. It's not a conventional live medium – this is a full local install, but shipped as an image of a USB key that you can boot and run. It comes with the Xfce desktop and an array of apps. The idea is that you can boot and run it on any x86-64 UEFI computer, entirely from a USB key, without touching the hard disk at all.

This is quite different from its forerunner, which is a relatively conventional Debian-based distro, one which The Register has mentioned a few times over the years: first back in 2015 in a lightweight distro roundup, and more recently in 2024 when we praised its array of desktop environments. Earlier this year, we noted that the latest SparkyLinux featured a complete 32-bit edition, even though its parent distro has dropped its 32-bit x86 kernel.

This is also not your typical live distro. Unless you're running on some Arm computer with nonstandard firmware, most Linux distros install from an image written to a USB pendrive, the same way that they did decades ago: in the noughties when they installed from a DVD, and back in the 20th century, when it was a CD instead. Most optical media use some form of the ISO standard 9660 filesystem, which is quite limited – despite multiple extensions, the core is a basic structure comparable to the ancient MS-DOS FAT. That's not much use for Linux, which needs long filenames, permissions, and metadata, plus things like symbolic links.

So, to this day, most live Linux media have a few boot files and the OS itself is kept inside a big compressed file called a SquashFS, inside which is a real Linux filesystem. However, because it's inside something akin to a Zip file, it's read-only. You can't update the OS or add new software. Some live media optionally offer persistence, which stores changes in another separate file. That works, but if you update the OS, all the original pre-update files remain untouched, and new ones are stored in the persistence structure in addition to the space still consumed by the originals. So, it's slow, and it's very inefficient; it takes substantially more space than a conventional disk install.

So, although there are dozens, maybe hundreds, of live Linux media images out there, most fall into one of two types of single-purpose product: either stripped-out special-purpose distros, such as SystemRescue, GParted Live, and Grml, or Rescuezilla, or Clonezilla. Alternatively, it's a full OS, but only meant as a sampler, not for daily use, with limited and inefficient tools for updates and changes. We're not sure if twice counts as a FAQ, but there are questions on StackExchange on how to install Ubuntu to USB as well as how to install Debian to USB.

SparkyOS is an answer to this question. It's a complete, pre-configured installation of Arch, directly onto a USB key. That does impose some limits, so for instance, like the Desktop Classic System we looked at in January, it only includes UEFI boot files. You can't use it on a computer with just a "legacy" BIOS, and it requires format conversion to use it in a VM.

The current SparkyOS version 2026.10 is the first release, but there are already some How-to documentation pages covering things like expanding the filesystem to fill the USB medium, changing its settings, and how to crowbar it into a VM. The image is 10 GB in size, compressed to 3.2 GB for download, and because this is an image of an entire key, it won't work with multiboot tools such as Reg FOSS desk favorite Ventoy. We put it onto a 64 GB key, and we chose one that has two connectors for both USB-A and USB-C ports. We tested it on our oldest UEFI box, a 15-year-old Thinkpad W520, and our newest UEFI testbed, a Dell XPS13 new enough that it only has USB-C ports.

We would suggest a USB 3 key, though, and use a blue-colored USB-A port if you have one. It will run on a USB-2 only machine, but a bit slower. We tried it on our X220, currently running OpenBSD 8.0, and it worked fine. It could even see OpenBSD’s 10 separate partitions, although not mount them. SparkyOS worked flawlessly on all three machines.

The team has made some concessions to running from USB flash media. The root volume is mounted with the noatime parameter, which stops Linux from recording the last access time on files. That dramatically lowers the number of writes to the drive. There’s also no swap configured – to our surprise, not even ZRAM, which doesn’t touch the disk.

SparkyOS does what it says: it's a complete, very usable, ready-to-run Linux OS, as fully capable of being updated, customized, and having apps added or removed as any other distro… running off a pendrive. We do suggest a big fast key, though, and don't fill it up. Flash isn't like RAM: you can't change a single byte, or word, at a time. Flash can only erase a whole block at a time, and block sizes vary from 16 kB for the smallest flash chips, up to multiple megabytes. To rewrite one byte on a flash drive, the storage controller has to copy a megabyte or more of data elsewhere, format the block, and then copy it back. So, leaving more free space on a flash drive gives the on-device storage-management chip more room to work. The more free space there is on a flash drive, the longer it will last.

This is one reason flash-based SSDs wear out – and also why we wrote that the end of Optane was bad news for the whole industry. SSDs often have multiple, high-speed flash chips on. Pendrives don't – there’s usually just one.

In a previous life, over a decade and a half ago, this vulture had a small startup company, and one of our products was a live Linux-based OS, pre-installed on bootable USB keys. I did everything I could to reduce writes to the drive: they were formatted with journalling disabled, mounted with noatime, with ZRAM for swap, the temporary-files directory kept in a RAMdisk, and more. The keys sold quite well, but one of the problems was that despite all my precautions, heavy users found that the drives simply wore out.

Flash media do not fail in the same way that industry old-timers know from spinning hard disks. A dying hard disk often struggles on, just with some blocks unreadable. That’s why tools such as GNU ddrescue exist – to try to copy the data off the regions that still work. When flash media fail, they tend to fail totally: you can't read from the device at all, meaning that nothing can be recovered from them.

An example of a fairly extreme adaptation in this direction is the FreeBSD-based XigmaNAS OS. In its Embedded installation mode on a flash drive, it writes its log files to a RAM drive to prevent wear to the flash. (The snag being that they are lost when it reboots.) A user add-on for to the proprietary unRAID NAS OS does the same.

There's room for future enhancements to SparkyOS here. Booting from both BIOS and UEFI is already on the "to do" list at the bottom of the release announcement. Additionally, steps to keep any files the OS writes to in RAM, and only write them out to flash at shutdown time, and so on.

But saying all that, it's here, it works, and it already looks like a handy tool if you regularly use multiple different computers and want to carry your own environment around with you. For routine use, though, use a big fast drive, connect it to USB-3 or USB-C ports whenever possible, and ensure it stays mostly empty — keep it under 50 percent full. Most importantly of all, regularly back up any data you keep on it. ®
